content.title: About
content.content: White cooked rice (NS) is a processed grain from which the outer layers (bran and germ) have been removed. After cooking it becomes soft, slightly sticky, and has a neutral flavor, making it a versatile base for many dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.
White rice has a longer shelf life than whole‑grain rice because the oily germ has been removed.
In Japan rice is often used for sushi‑rice, which is seasoned with vinegar, sugar, and salt after cooking.
In China rice is traditionally served as “congee,” where the grains stay separate and fluffy.
Rice can be grown in flooded paddies, which helps control weeds.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: White rice is rich in carbohydrates that quickly convert to glucose, providing a rapid energy boost.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The lack of bran makes cooked white rice gentle on the digestive tract, suitable for diets after gastrointestinal upset.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: A 100 g serving of cooked rice contains less than 0.5 g of fat, fitting low‑fat eating plans.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice provides thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are involved in carbohydrate metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Magnesium, phosphorus and iron in rice support muscle function and blood health.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: The removal of bran makes rice less beneficial for digestion compared with whole‑grain cereals.

items.title: Arsenic presence
items.content: In some regions rice may contain trace arsenic; rinsing the rice before cooking is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice can be served as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables, used in soups, pilafs, sushi, rice salads, or as a base for risotto. For added flavor, cook rice in broth or add herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and kept in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days, or frozen for longer storage.
